shouldFix.title: d9Code, hostTermination and planAdmission are named prohibitions with no retained class, and the D9/exit class present in v1 was removed
shouldFix.finding: refusal.namedInstances lists eleven prohibited items. Mapping each against the five retained classes: finding/findingLikeResult is covered by NT-1, NT-2 and NT-3; policyOutcome, verdict, threshold, waiver and gate by NT-2 and NT-4; the Coverage-domain family by NT-5. d9Code, hostTermination and planAdmission map to nothing. NT-2's added-member roster is closed — findings, finding, verdict, threshold, waiver — and does not include a D9 class or a HostTermination, and NT-4's roster is policyOutcome, verdict, threshold, waiver and gate. This is a regression rather than an inherited gap: v1 carried NT-3 'component-emits-d9-or-exit-refused' whose input was 'a payload that includes a D9 class, exit number, or HostTermination' and whose pass condition was 'No D9 code is minted from the component. Existing v1.14 mapping remains host-owned.' v2 rebuilt the class list around the wire and dropped that class without replacement, while keeping d9Code and hostTermination in the prohibition list. The prohibition it leaves untested is the one DR-007 guards most directly: the register records that row's blueprint impact as 'V2 cannot define replay/purge/degradation typed result or exit', and file 01's Finalization/D9 row makes 'select public success/error/exit' something the component must never do.
shouldFix.whyNotBlocking: The refusal rule is total, so these items are refused by the operative law even without a class; and the acceptance cell's literal test obligation is about findings, which NT-1 through NT-3 cover well. The defect is retained-evidence coverage of the artifact's own prohibition list, plus the loss of a class the predecessor had.
shouldFix.repair: Restore a D9/exit class in the v2 idiom — a constructible member or frame carrying a D9 class, exit number or HostTermination, rejected before admission with no D9 minted from the component — and add a class for planAdmission, so every named instance has a retained class.

shouldFix.title: The totality inversion is type-level, but two of the five retained classes test content-level violations inside admitted types
shouldFix.finding: refusal.rule reads: 'Total. Any TypeScript provider output that is not (a) an admitted semantic output or (b) an admitted existing protocol frame needed to carry those outputs is refused before admission. The forbidden enumeration below is named instances, not the trigger.' admittedSemanticOutputs is a type list — semanticFact and coverage — so the trigger reads as type-level membership. Two retained classes then test violations that occur inside an admitted type rather than outside the set. NT-5's input is 'A Coverage payload that narrows, widens, or converts unknown to covered relative to the host-requested domain': a Coverage payload is an admitted semantic output, so limb (a) is satisfied and the total rule does not fire. NT-3's input is a FactCandidateV1 whose relationSchemaId or payload is provider-minted or mismatched: the carrier is an admitted fact-candidate, so again limb (a) is satisfied. For both, the prohibition survives only through namedInstances — which the same sentence says is 'not the trigger'. That is a narrower recurrence of the v1 defect at the type/content seam: the enumeration is doing operative work the rule disclaims.
shouldFix.whyNotBlocking: Unlike v1 there is no unspecified region — the prohibitions are stated in namedInstances, tested by NT-3 and NT-5, and reinforced by hostOwned's admissionOfFacts and admissionOfCoverage. This is an ambiguity about which clause generates the refusal, not a missing disposition.
shouldFix.repair: Split the rule in two: a type-level limb refusing any output outside the admitted set, and a content-level limb stating that an output of an admitted type is admitted only if it passes host validation — the relation/schema registry for fact candidates, and domain conformance without unknown-to-covered conversion for Coverage — with anything failing that validation refused before admission. That makes NT-3 and NT-5 consequences of the rule rather than of the enumeration.

coordinatorSummary: REJECT at 0 blockers and 3 SHOULD-FIX, with 1 advisory. Sixteen attacks run, four landed, none at blocker grade. Custody is intact: subject e91595a0 at 0444 unmoved and valid JSON, predecessor v1 frozen at 237efad5, HEAD never left 52ea851, file 08 and COORD at their pins with a clean tree. All three v1 blockers are repaired, and I tested each against live sources rather than against my own earlier text. CLAUDE-POOC-V1-B1 is repaired thoroughly: file 01 is cited by path and digest with its section and closing sentence verbatim, the narrowing is scoped to the D-002 preview TypeScript provider role and declared a recorded delta, and the kept-plus-removed lists partition file 01's seven may-return entries exactly — six kept, one removed, nothing invented — with the hostOwned incoherence I flagged resolved. CLAUDE-POOC-V1-B2 is repaired: the rule now opens 'Total.', keys refusal to absence from the admitted set, demotes the enumeration to named instances, and adds thresholds, waivers, gate and the Coverage-domain family. Codex's POOCV1-B1 is repaired: I resolved the wire to delivery.v2.json and confirmed all nine worker-to-host frame names plus FactCandidateV1, FactBatchV1 and relationSchemaId exist there, so the rebuilt classes — out-of-vocabulary frame, added member on a closed payload, FactCandidate relationSchemaId masquerade — are constructible, and findingLikeResult is now defined by property. What remains is additive. First, three named prohibitions have no retained class — d9Code, hostTermination and planAdmission — and this is a regression: v1 carried a component-emits-d9-or-exit class and v2 dropped it while keeping the prohibitions, leaving untested the boundary DR-007 guards most directly. Second, the totality inversion is type-level while two of the five classes test content-level violations inside admitted types: a domain-mutating Coverage and a masquerading FactCandidate both satisfy limb (a), so their prohibition survives only through the enumeration the rule says is not the trigger. Third, the wire is the one governing source left unpinned, in an artifact that pins the other three by digest, and it is precisely the source that carries the Codex repair; DELIVERY's standing is contested at DR-011-R04, so which bytes are meant is worth stating. The advisory is that v1's identityDependencies routing to DR-006, D-077 and D-078 was dropped with no successor. None of the three findings requires restructuring; a v3 that restores and adds two test classes, splits the rule into type and content limbs, and pins the wire should ACCEPT.
